name: AutoCAD
tagline: Professional 2D drafting and 3D CAD software with the DWG file format at its center.

pricing.basis: per user subscription, monthly or annual
pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: An agent can absolutely give you a canvas with lines, arcs, layers, snapping and dimension text in an afternoon, and for sketching a shelf bracket that is genuinely enough. What it cannot give you is a hardened geometry kernel, a constraint solver, DWG read/write that other people trust, or forty years of accumulated commands that drafters have in muscle memory. The actual job of AutoCAD is handing a file to a fabricator, a contractor, or a plan reviewer and having it open correctly on their machine, which is a file-format and liability problem, not a drawing problem. Break the DWG round trip and the tool is useless for work even if the drawing looks fine on your screen. Build the sketchpad if you want one, but do not pretend it replaces the seat.
coreLoopDIY: A local browser drafting pad: draw lines, polylines, arcs and circles on a grid with snapping and layers, add linear dimensions, save to JSON and export DXF.
requirements: A DXF writer library for export
whatYouLose: DWG read and write, so nobody else can open your files reliably
Parametric constraints and a real solver, your geometry drifts by hand
Blocks, xrefs, layouts, plot styles, sheet sets, and printing to scale
Every industry toolset, template library, and the plugin ecosystem around them
moatNotes: DWG is the lingua franca of the construction and manufacturing supply chain, and the readers that matter are the ones Autodesk ships.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the drawing is a deliverable that leaves your computer. A contractor, machine shop, or permit office expects a DWG that opens cleanly, prints to scale, and matches the title block conventions everyone already uses, and if it does not the delay costs more than the seat. On top of that, drafters are fast in AutoCAD in a way that took years to build, and retraining a team onto a homemade canvas is a real payroll expense. The subscription is annoying, widely resented, and still cheaper than being the person whose file nobody can open.
notes: A drawing canvas is a weekend; a CAD system is not. The moat is DWG interchange plus the entire construction and manufacturing supply chain agreeing to speak it.
prompt:
Build a local, offline 2D drafting sketchpad. Consolation prize for AutoCAD, not a clone.

Stack, no substitutions: Vite + TypeScript, plain DOM, HTML canvas 2D. No React, no backend, no accounts, no telemetry, no cloud. Everything runs from `npm run dev` and persists to IndexedDB.

In scope:
- Infinite pan/zoom canvas with a configurable grid and world units in millimeters.
- Draw tools: line, polyline, rectangle, circle, arc (three point).
- Snapping: grid, endpoint, midpoint, center, intersection, plus orthogonal lock while a modifier key is held. Show a snap marker.
- Coordinate entry: while a tool is active, allow typing numeric length and angle to place the next point exactly.
- Selection with click and rubber band box. Move, copy, rotate, mirror, delete, trim to nearest intersection.
- Layers panel: name, color, visibility, lock. New entities go on the current layer.
- Linear and aligned dimensions plus single line text annotations. Dimensions store references to their endpoints and update when the geometry moves.
- Undo/redo over a flat command history, at least 100 steps.
- Save/load named drawings in IndexedDB, plus export and import a plain JSON document format.
- Export DXF (R12 style, LINE/CIRCLE/ARC/LWPOLYLINE/TEXT, layers preserved) using a DXF writer library from npm. Import is not required.
- Print to a chosen paper size at a chosen scale via a print stylesheet.

Out of scope, do not attempt: DWG, 3D, solids, constraint solving, blocks, xrefs, hatching, multiplayer.

Architecture: a single document model of typed entities with stable ids, a pure geometry module with unit tests for intersection, snapping and trim math, and a renderer that redraws from the model each frame. Keep geometry math out of the UI code.

Deliver a README stating plainly that DXF export is lossy and this is not a substitute for a real CAD seat.
